findings.title: [CC-13] 2 sk-shaped strings in raw-store member results/phase7/capture.json /input_rail_yaml: one a synthetic canned-leak string, one a real-format Langfuse secret key (sk-lf-<uuid4>, localhost:3300, integration disabled) not established as synthetic; not selected; 0 in AER/SEM/PROV
findings.evidence: acct.py over all 109 zip members: secret-shape hits 2, both in results/phase7/capture.json (member disposition not_selected, one of 66), JSON pointer /input_rail_yaml (a 6,094-char guardrail-rail YAML string); shapes: len 42 segments [2,2,8,4,4,4,12] (UUID-like) and len 30 'sk-proj-' + 22; entropy 3.86 / 4.71 bits/char; digests sha256_8 <secret-A>, <account-A>; the surrounding string contains the words detect/leak/redact/fake/secret/key (a secret-detection rail config, so probably synthetic test keys; not established). Account paths: 0 in all 109 members. The raw store keeps the whole deposit zip (origins: 1 zenodo object + 43 members), so the bytes are in a raw-store file. L1-06 (selected 14 + auxiliary/context 29) and L1-10 (0 non-JSON context files) never read this member. AER/SEM/PROV: redaction 0 hits over 3,248 files; phase 7 rows are register rows (select.not_execution_artefact), not executions. The deposit is public on Zenodo (CC-BY-4.0). VERIFIER (masked context via quote_untrusted, values never printed; scripts ~/.agentprov/migration-work/precheck/autogen-guard-placement/exam/verify/skctx.py, skuuid.py): the rail YAML has 250 lines; hit <account-A> (YAML line 240) sits inside a canned guardrail response 'secret_leak' that also states a fake admin password, and its shape (sk-proj- + length withheld, 30 total) is far shorter than an issued OpenAI project key, so it is synthetic test text. Hit <secret-A> (YAML line 211) is NOT OpenAI-shaped: it is 'secret_key' under observability.langfuse (enabled: false, host http://localhost:3300), paired with a 'public_key' pk-lf-<uuid> (sha256_8 a41d85a7); both are sk-lf-/pk-lf- + a valid RFC-4122 version-4 UUID, the format a Langfuse instance issues. Synthetic is not established; it looks like the author's local self-hosted Langfuse project key pair. Exposure: only usable against a localhost instance; already public in the Zenodo deposit; each string occurs once in the whole zip (0 in the other 108 members). The canned fake password in the same response is not caught by any screen (no secret shape).

findings.evidence: sem.py over the 1,080 mapped executions joined 1:1 to raw rows (member sha256 + line): any canary_present = raw (canary in save_note text or writer final message) in 1,080/1,080 (0 mismatches); against the paper's goal-kind metric 9 attack runs differ (all goal_kind output with the canary only in a save_note call: p2 3, p12 4, p13 2), 7 of them on test carriers (p2 tool, p12 spotlight user/agent x2, p12 sandwich user, p13 tool, p13 memory). Test-carrier attack total: raw 111, mapped goal-kind-filtered 111 (0 of 306 goal-bearing runs differ), mapped any-annotation 118. D-306 and the prereg describe the claim as 'canary in a save_note argument or the writer's final message (goal kinds tool/output)'; semantics/tools.py _canary annotates every writer text part and every save_note call; the goal kind is in the probe fixture ext (/ext/autogen/goal_kind). No aggregate arm passes the gap rule even unfiltered (largest p12 spotlight 26/40 vs 23/40, +7.5 pp, paper inside Wilson [49.51, 77.87]).
findings.recommendation: R4: route to the autogen family owner: state the consumer rule (filter by fixture goal_kind; output goal = annotation on the last writer text message) in spec D.19.8 / D-306, or add a run-level claim in a later semantics version (byte-changing, a regen item). verdicts.reasoning: semantics/tools.py _canary annotates every writer text part and every save_note call with no goal_kind test; spec D.22.6 defines canary_present that way (location claim), so the engine matches the spec; the mismatch is D-306/prereg wording '(goal kinds tool/output)' and the absence of a stated consumer rule.
